summary:
Iteration 9 tested end-to-end. Backend: 28/29 pytest pass (~10s) in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration9.py covering Gazetteer (search, typo tolerance, KG basin, netherlands, types, admin create/delete flow, invalid type/bbox 400, seed protection 404), Historical Archive (12 seeded incidents inc. Deepwater Horizon/X-Press Pearl/Dawn Kanchipuram, chennai filter, analyst 403, supervisor create+delete, bad date 400, seed protected, /precedents returns 3 with similarity+distance_km and correct weights), Playbook (advisory:true, version, disclaimer, all inputs incl. estimated_volume_tonnes{sheen,thin,thick}, 4 tactical coords for SPL-001, 3 tiers with tier2.dispersant/in_situ_burning/bioremediation objects, unknown case 404, evidence.pdf still 200), Prosecution Export (analyst 403; supervisor 200 application/zip w/ X-Bundle-SHA256 + X-Export-Id; MANIFEST.json + required files evidence.pdf/case.json/ais_fixes.json/correlation_results.json/audit_history.json/remediation_playbook.json present; per-file sha256 match; list-exports endpoint returns record; audit_history contains case.prosecution_exported), Verify (PUBLIC GET /verify/{hash} verified true matched=bundle, deadbeef -> verified false unknown_hash, PUBLIC POST /verify with untouched zip -> status verified, tampered zip with modified case.json -> status tampered with case.json ok:false, zip w/o MANIFEST -> invalid_bundle). Single failing test: q='bombay' surfaces 'Cambay Basin' first (WRatio tie 60.0 with 'Bombay High' due to spelling proximity) — Bombay High only surfaces cleanly on 'bombay high' or 'bombay hgih' typo (73.6). Minor fuzzy-weighting issue only.

Frontend (Playwright on public URL): (a) PUBLIC /verify page loads without auth; unknown hash 'deadbeef*8' -> verify-status 'NOT VERIFIED — unknown_hash'. (b) Supervisor login OK; nav-archive-link -> archive-page with archive-count '12 incidents', archive-search 'chennai' -> URL adds q=chennai and count drops to '1 incidents'; btn-archive-add visible for supervisor, clicking reveals archive-form. (c) Scene Explorer asset-search-input visible; typing 'Bombay' -> asset-search-results with 3 asset-hit-* cards. (d) Case SPL-20260610-001 detail: tab-response shows playbook-panel + playbook-advisory + playbook-inputs + playbook-tier1/2/3 + playbook-tactical + precedents-drawer with 3 precedent-* cards; asset-search-input present on case; supervisor sees btn-prosecution-export, clicking triggers download of 'SPL-20260610-001_prosecution.zip'. (e) Regression navigation (/, /events, /compare, /explorer) loads clean.

BUG FOUND & FIXED: CaseDetail.jsx threw ReferenceError 'hasRole is not defined' and 'user is not defined' → prosecution-export gating references (line 124) never imported hasRole/useAuth. Added imports `hasRole` from @/lib/api and `useAuth` from @/context/AuthContext + destructured user. Without the fix the entire /cases/:id page crashed with an Uncaught runtime error red overlay — every iteration-9 UI feature (playbook, precedents, asset-search on case, export button) was blocked. Fix verified — page now renders correctly and all iteration-9 selectors resolve.

minor.issue: Fuzzy WRatio scorer surfaces 'Cambay Basin' as the top hit (match 60.0) and 'Bombay High (Mumbai High) oil field' either ties or is excluded by score_cutoff=55 depending on the search corpus. Task expected Bombay High to be first for q='bombay'. Suggest scoring the name token separately (or boosting exact-substring 'bombay') so that 'bombay' surfaces Bombay High above Cambay. Typo 'bombay hgih' works fine (73.6).

ui_bugs.issue: Uncaught ReferenceError 'hasRole is not defined' — every case detail page crashed with the red overlay because line 124 (btn-prosecution-export gate) called hasRole(user, 'supervisor') but neither hasRole nor user were imported into the module. Fixed in this iteration by adding `hasRole` to the @/lib/api import and `useAuth` from @/context/AuthContext + `const { user } = useAuth()` inside the component.

issues: React hydration warning still present: '<span> option cannot be a child of <span>' — unchanged.
Non-blocking Recharts warning 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0…' triggers on initial mount before container measures. Cosmetic — chart renders correctly after layout.

action_items: (Minor) Reweight gazetteer fuzzy search so that a single-word query matches the token in `name` more strongly — currently 'bombay' surfaces 'Cambay Basin' ahead of 'Bombay High'. Options: score name/country/operator/type independently and take max, or add substring boost for exact case-insensitive contains-in-name.

(Optional) Add an ErrorBoundary around <CaseDetail> so a single reference/render error in any tab doesn't wipe the whole page — the missing-import bug produced a full red-screen overlay instead of a scoped fallback.
(Carry-over) Fix the '<option> cannot be a child of <span>' hydration warning in the Layout header (still present from iter 7).
critical_code_review_comments: routers/gazetteer.py: `_entries()` merges seeded gazetteer + active jurisdictions (as type=eez). The search uses rapidfuzz WRatio which is token-set-aware — good for typos but tends to score short queries lower against long names. Consider `process.extract(q, keys, scorer=fuzz.partial_ratio)` as a fallback tier, or splitting into name-scorer + metadata-scorer with max().
routers/gazetteer.py delete: correctly protects seed rows via `source: {$ne: 'seed'}` filter; returns 404 both for missing IDs and seed IDs — acceptable (obfuscates seed existence).

routers/archive.py POST: catches `ValueError` around _doc() to convert bad date -> 400, but _doc() only calls datetime.fromisoformat(date). If any other field raises ValueError (e.g. malformed number cast upstream) the 'date must be ISO YYYY-MM-DD' message would be misleading. Pydantic-level date validation would be cleaner.

routers/archive.py precedents: volume estimate `(area × 1e6 × 1e-6 × 0.9 × 1000 / 1000)` simplifies to `area × 0.9` tonnes assuming 1 µm thickness — the note in the comment matches but the formula is unnecessarily obfuscated. Consider a named helper.

playbook.py coast_distance_km: radial land-mask search in 15° increments across up to 300 km — correct for order-of-magnitude estimates. Note: the returned coast_distance quantizes to the ring radii list [1,2,5,10,15,20,30,40,50,75,100,150,200,300], so downstream ETA calculations are coarse. Acceptable for advisory purposes; label 'approximate' already conveyed in disclaimer.

playbook.py build_playbook: `wind, current = A if C else B, X if C else Y` chained-assignment pattern is a Python precedence footgun — parses correctly here because both RHS are complete expressions, but a future edit could easily break it. Recommend split into two explicit statements.

routers/prosecution.py export: manifest content_hash covers file names + per-file sha256 (sorted) — solid design; bundle_sha256 = SHA-256 of the zip bytes. Both are indexed for /verify lookup via $or. Non-blocking observation: repeated exports for the same case accumulate rows in prosecution_exports with no de-dup — expected (evidence lifecycle) but should be surfaced in the UI list.

routers/prosecution.py verify_upload: MANIFEST hash re-derivation is deterministic and matches export path. Correctly distinguishes verified / content_verified_repackaged / tampered / unknown_export / invalid_bundle. Public endpoint (no auth) — correct for prosecutorial verification workflow. Rate-limiting would be a nice-to-have but not required.

frontend CaseDetail.jsx (CRITICAL, fixed): hasRole/user references without imports crashed the whole page. Suggest ESLint react/react-in-jsx-scope + no-undef in CI to catch this class of regression before deploy.
frontend Verify.jsx uses axios directly with `${process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL}/api` — correct for a route that must work without a session cookie / bearer token.

seed_data_creation: Backend tests create and delete a TEST_iter9_asset gazetteer row (admin) and a TEST_iter9_spill archive row (supervisor) within their tests — both cleaned up in the same test. Prosecution export test triggers a real export on SPL-20260610-001 which persists a record in db.prosecution_exports (used by /verify) — this is by design (immutable audit ledger) and stacks on prior iterations' exports.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run backend: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration9.py -v -o addopts='' --tb=short. BASE_URL is read from /app/frontend/.env. Gotchas: (1) after writing a new file into /app/backend/tests/*.py, uvicorn hot-reloads; first login POST may hit read-timeout — wait ~8s and retry. (2) db.prosecution_exports is an append-only ledger, so re-running the export test grows it linearly. (3) The gazetteer q='bombay' -> Cambay-first behavior is a real fuzzy-scorer quirk, not a test flake. (4) /verify (both GET/hash and POST/upload) are PUBLIC — no auth header required. (5) The CaseDetail hasRole ReferenceError fix in this iteration is trivial (2-line import) but was blocking every case-detail page; if you see the red-overlay 'Uncaught runtime error' page, check imports on any newly-added JSX that references hasRole/user. (6) SPL-20260610-001 case_id is looked up via GET /api/cases search — do not hardcode the UUID.
rca_of_the_issue: CaseDetail.jsx line 124 was added in iteration 9 to gate the new btn-prosecution-export behind supervisor role: `{hasRole(user, 'supervisor') && <button ...>}`. However, the file previously only imported `{ api, apiError, fmtTime, pct }` from '@/lib/api' and never called useAuth() — so both `hasRole` and `user` were undefined at render, causing a synchronous ReferenceError. Impact: every /cases/:id page rendered a red uncaught-runtime-error overlay. Reproduction: log in as any role → click any case number → runtime error overlay appears (before hitting any Response tab). Mitigation applied: `import { api, apiError, fmtTime, pct, hasRole } from '@/lib/api'; import { useAuth } from '@/context/AuthContext';` and `const { user } = useAuth();` inside the component. Verified post-fix: all iteration-9 case-detail selectors (playbook-*, precedents-drawer, precedent-* cards, asset-search-input, btn-prosecution-export) resolve and the export click downloads the zip.
